t.E553a.agn: In 2018, EFSA saw no indication of genotoxicity or developmental toxicity for calcium and magnesium silicate and talc; however, noting that accumulation of silicon from calcium silicate in the kidney and liver of rats had been reported and that there were no reliable long-term toxicity, carcinogenicity and reproductive data, it concluded that their safety as additives could not be assessed. It stated that the group ADI set by the SCF in 1991 for silicon dioxide and silicates was no longer valid. It also noted that magnesium trisilicate has been used for decades as a stomach medicine at up to 4 g per day and that there were no confirmed cases of kidney effects in the EU pharmacovigilance database.
t.E553a.eff.0.t: EFSA could not assess its safety because there are no reliable long-term toxicity, carcinogenicity and reproductive data
t.E553a.found.0: Powdered foods, sliced or grated cheese, foods in tablet form and food supplements (E 551–553 group)
t.E553a.prod: It is a chemically produced silicate.
t.E553a.regx.0: Re-evaluated; safety could not be assessed due to lack of data; the SCF group ADI was considered no longer valid.
t.E553a.regx.1: Permitted at specified levels in powdered and tablet-form foods, cheese, salt, seasonings, chewing gum surfaces and food supplements (E 551–553 group).
t.E553a.summary: Magnesium silicate. It prevents caking in powdered products.
t.E553a.what: It is magnesium silicate and magnesium trisilicate, which prevent caking of powdered foods.
